text:
Sínann is an Irish river goddess. She rules the River Shannon, the great waterway that cuts across Ireland. Her name gives the river its power and its place in legend. In the tales she is counted among the river goddesses of the Celts, alongside Bóand, who gives her name to the River Boyne.

The central story of Sínann concerns wisdom. A secret well of wisdom lay beneath the white mountain Cuilcagh in County Cavan. In that pool swam the salmon of wisdom. Sínann caught the salmon and ate it. As the fish's wisdom flooded into her, the well rose up and drowned her, taking the wisdom with her.

Two readings of the tale survive. Some read it as a warning against women who seek wisdom. Others read it as a creation myth, in which the goddess gives herself to form a great river. The same story is told of Bóand, making the one well the source of two of Ireland's most important rivers.
